d: A cyst in a persisting segment of the duct the thyroid follows as it descends from the foramen cecum; it sits in the midline and rises with swallowing or tongue protrusion.
Neural crest cells that reach the thyroid through the fourth pouch ultimobranchial body and secrete calcitonin; they give rise to medullary thyroid carcinoma.
The basolateral follicular-cell transporter that concentrates iodide using the sodium gradient; perchlorate and pertechnetate compete with iodide for it, and TSH increases its expression.
The apical enzyme that oxidizes iodide, attaches it to tyrosines on thyroglobulin and couples iodotyrosines into T4 and T3; methimazole and propylthiouracil inhibit it.
The tissue enzyme that removes an outer-ring iodine to convert T4 into active T3; propylthiouracil, propranolol, glucocorticoids, amiodarone and severe illness inhibit it.
The brief shutdown of organification after a large iodide load, which protects against hormone excess; a damaged gland may fail to escape and become hypothyroid.
The liver protein that carries most circulating T4; estrogen raises it, while androgens, nephrotic syndrome and liver failure lower it, changing total but not free T4.
An inactive product made when an inner-ring iodine is removed from T4; it rises in severe illness while active T3 falls.
